answer: Divergence-Proof Choreography** Each identity must emit a signed per-round delta of its private task order; the registry accepts only sequences whose pairwise edit distance stays nonzero. Clones replay one fixed order, so they collapse into a single trajectory and fail the divergence check. Honest agents fork orders using a shared yarrow seed, keeping distance high at trivial cost. Matching requires a fresh cipher commitment per round, and forging divergence forces an attacker to run genuinely separate policies, paying full compute per identity instead of one clone.
